body:
## collections-sot — labelled entities on the worldline spine

Contracts/collections become **labelled entities on the same hash-chained shadow-mode ledger as the member graph** (the operator's reframe: labelling members and labelling contract addresses are ONE substrate). The append-only observation chain is the source of truth; the entity projection is a re-fold. The full derive-don't-ask loop:

```
belt + ERC-165 + world ──▶ distill ──▶ propose (born-low) ──▶ ratify (cockpit grant) ──▶ shadow-audit serves it
   raw signals          ground     ai-derived/unread      subjective-only, force-chain    settle gate, fail-closed
```

### Supersedes #429
This branch **merges the sandwich-line spine (#429)** — collections-sot consumes it (hash chain + producer-auth + shadow-audit collections read), and the worktree only held a broken partial leak of it. `#429`'s CI redness is unrelated pre-existing monolith failures (a sietch webhook flake being fixed on its own branch + an `aws-embedded-metrics` dep issue); the spine's own tests pass. Merging this closes #429's work.

### What's here (295 tests, 0 typecheck errors)
- **S1** — identity choke point (`collectionEntityId`), `CollectionEntity` + content-addressed `collection.label.{observed,ratified}` factories, store fold (chain=SoT, projection=fold, verify-on-read). `SubjectKind += 'collection'` (additive; member subjects untouched).
- **S2** — distiller `ground()` (belt GraphQL + ERC-165 dependency-free raw `eth_call`, injectable FR-7 seam) reproduces the 24-collection proof (20 erc721 + 4 erc1155) with zero operator input; `propose` (born-low); `ratify` gated by a single-consume cockpit grant (`~/.claude/.recall-cockpit-grant`), subjective labels only.
- **S3** — `query` (lexical + provenance badge, contested-withheld like /recall); **settle gate** — shadow-audit reads the ratified snapshot fail-closed (`COLLECTION_REGISTRY` env → deprecated break-glass), the G-4 kill-test passes; drift sensor; 6-verb agent-first CLI + live belt/RPC clients.

### Fail-closed / trust invariants
- The chain is the trust root: `getCollectionEntity`/`listCollectionEntities` verify-on-read (a tampered chain is refused/excluded, never served).
- Ratify flips `ai-derived → operator-validated` ONLY via a fresh single-consume grant; derived labels are never ratifiable; a member subject can't be collection-ratified.
- The settle gate serves a collection ONLY when standard ∈ {erc721,erc1155} AND world is operator-validated AND not contested; a missing/malformed snapshot fails loud.
- Drift never re-contests an operator-validated label (respects settled truth).

### Two self-review passes (FAGAN) on the diff, both addressed
- **S1**: a ratify on a derived label appended as attested truth but the fold silently ignored it → fail-closed reject at construction.
- **S2/S3**: a merge-blocker where drift re-proposed the world heuristic every run and would re-contest ratified truth forever → drift never touches an operator-validated label; world heuristic narrowed to an explicit allowlist; cockpit grant made fail-closed on unlink failure.

### Remaining (deploy-only, not in this PR's domain logic)
- Point shadow-audit's `COLLECTION_SNAPSHOT_PATH` at a `collections export-snapshot` build step.
- 7 skipped tests are Postgres integration (need a live DB in CI).
- QMD-source registration of the entity export (documented seam, next cycle).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Bridgebuilder findings — triage + resolution (commit 0dea3091)

Thanks — the two HIGH findings were exactly right. Addressed:

**Fixed (this PR):**
- **CSOT-001 (HIGH)** — `drift` now never lets `unknown` overwrite a *known* `token_standard`. Your Kafka-idempotency parallel nailed it: a transient RPC blip degrading to `unknown` would dedup a later re-derive (content-addressed `event_id`) and strand the entity at `unknown` forever, silently ejecting it from the settle gate. Invariant added: no-information never overwrites information. Regression test covers RPC-down → recovers → stays `erc721`. (The general A→B→A for `collection_key` remains a documented content-addressing limitation; belt keys are stable, and the monotonic-id upgrade is noted for when a real oscillation appears.)
- **CSOT-002 (HIGH)** — the pg store now canonicalizes timestamps (`toISOString`) **before** hashing + storing, so a `timestamptz` round-trip can't falsely freeze a healthy chain. In-memory was already self-consistent, so CI (in-memory) was unaffected — this closes the Postgres member-path hole you found.
- **CSOT-003 (MED)** — `consumeCockpitGrant` now unlinks **without** `force`, so the unlink itself is the atomic race winner (ENOENT → not authorized); `force:true` had masked a lost race.
- **CSOT-004 (MED)** — read verbs (`query`, `export-snapshot`) no longer run DDL migrations.
- **CSOT-011 (LOW)** — `drift` `drifted` is no longer clobbered by `unknown_standard`.

**Triaged as pre-existing #429 spine (not this cycle; flagged for their own follow-up):**
- **CSOT-005** (O(chain) verify-on-read) — a deliberate correctness>perf tradeoff for the fail-closed settle gate; collection chains are short (a handful of labels). Incremental/checkpointed verify is a spine enhancement.
- **CSOT-006** (JWT missing `communities` → unrestricted) — real fail-open in the spine JWT policy; collections don't use the JWT path (module-mint grant). Changing #429's auth semantics deserves its own review, not a silent flip in a collections merge.
- **CSOT-007 / CSOT-008** (deep-import reaches `mintGrant`; chain-admin two-env ceremony) — spine hardening, pre-existing.
- **CSOT-010 (SPECULATION)** — differential `no_backfill_window` classification, sandwich-line S3.
- **CSOT-009 (LOW)** — belt-gateway default URL is already `BELT_GATEWAY_URL`-overridable; the default is the real endpoint.

The 3 PRAISE items (capability-based append auth, JCS loud-rejection, pg append sequencing) are all spine work from #429. Merging.

## Post-Merge: Simple Release

| Phase | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Semver | 7.57.0 (minor) |
| Tag | v7.57.0 |

### 💡 Codex Review Here are some automated review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `f8c5d94c5f`
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
[Your team has set up Codex to review pull requests in this repo](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/settings/general). Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. Codex can also answer questions or update the PR. Try commenting "@codex address that feedback".

## Summary

This PR lands a genuinely well-layered spine — content-addressed observations on a hash chain, capability-gated appends, and a fold that derives collection truth from the ledger. The append path, grant design, and JCS foundation are strong. The primary concerns are two HIGH correctness findings at the *derivation* layer: content-addressed dedup makes legitimate value re-assertion impossible (CSOT-001), and timestamp round-tripping through Postgres can freeze healthy chains as "tampered" (CSOT-002). Both are the classic failure mode of hash-based systems: hashing the wrong equivalence class.

## Architectural Meditation

There's a unifying thread across CSOT-001 and CSOT-002 worth naming: **a hash chain is only as sound as the byte-identity of what it hashes**. Certificate Transparency logs learned this early — they Merkle-hash the stored bytes and never a re-derivation, because any lossy round-trip (timestamps, encodings) turns "verify" into "guess whether serialization is stable." Meanwhile, Kafka's idempotent producer deliberately dedups on *sequence numbers* rather than payload content, precisely because identical payloads legitimately recur in real event streams. This PR made the opposite choice on both axes, and the two HIGH findings fall directly out of it. Neither is hard to fix now; both are miserable to fix after live producers exist.

The second thread: the read path quietly acquired write-path obligations (CSOT-004, CSOT-005). Fail-closed is the right instinct, but "fail closed" should mean *refuse to serve*, not *silently mutate state while serving a read*.

## Findings

- **[Quality] The JCS canonicalizer (CSOT-013)** refuses to hash what it can't canonicalize, tested against the RFC's own vectors. The irony worth savoring: applying this exact module's philosophy at the Postgres timestamp boundary is the fix for CSOT-002.
- **[Operational] The append transaction (CSOT-014)** sequences its lock, integrity check, and insert correctly, and — rarest of all — documents its known atomicity ceiling with a named upgrade trigger instead of hoping nobody notices.
